title: Linear-time directed shortest paths with positive integer weights
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic word-RAM algorithm which computes all single-source distances in every directed graph with positive integer edge weights in \(O(m+n)\) worst-case time?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with word length w, addressed word memory, addition and subtraction modulo \(2^{w}\), multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), Boolean bit operations, shifts by less than w, comparisons and conditional branches, each costing one step. No nonuniform tables are supplied; initialization and preprocessing are charged. The graph has vertex set \([n], m\) explicitly listed directed edges, a designated source s, and weights in \(\{1,\ldots ,2^{w}- 1\}\), with \(w\ge \lceil \log _{2}(n+m+2)\rceil\). Parallel edges and loops are allowed. A distance is the minimum sum of weights on a directed s-to-v path, or infinity if no such path exists. Finite distances can be represented in at most two words; output costs count. The algorithm must work for every w with a universal constant in \(O(m+n)\).

context_blocks.text: Positive weights make directed shortest paths a fundamental optimization primitive, yet direction obstructs the classical linear-time result for undirected integer-weighted graphs. The target removes all superlinear overhead in the integer RAM model.

Recent algorithms break the sorting barrier for directed real-weighted shortest paths. Their sublogarithmic overhead and the later almost-linear results are substantial advances, but neither “almost linear” nor “nearly linear” means \(O(m+n)\). This card fixes the weight representation and charges preprocessing.

why: Settle whether directed weighted reachability has the same input-linear cost as its basic unweighted counterpart in the integer model.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
